The reference is simply the four-tip section kept almost verbatim. Whitney's approved version retained her own wording, so the best candidate preserves it. Candidate A keeps the four tips in the same order and mostly in her wording. It adds Halloween-themed headers, which fit the email's tone, and compresses the third and fourth tips slightly. Some of the compression loses content: it drops "you don't need a massive budget; you just need a smart strategy," although it keeps the budget idea. A few edits would restore her wording. Candidate B rewrites the whole email, changes the subject and preview text, drops the Halloween and slay theme and the "killing it" voice, and rewrites each tip with new claims. It also changes the CTA structure and the positioning ("build your first campaigns for you... as you learn to manage yourself"). That is far from what she approved, so it would need many edits.

request.system:
You compare two draft pieces of marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), a wedding-industry advertising agency. You are given the request, the version WIA's co-founder Whitney actually approved or wrote (the reference), and two candidate drafts. Decide which candidate would need fewer and smaller edits to become something Whitney would approve. Judge substance first (what is claimed, for whom, how WIA is positioned, accuracy, whether her own wording was kept where she supplied it), then voice. Do not reward length, and do not require the candidate to copy the reference wording.

Return only JSON: {"winner": "A" or "B" or "tie", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "one or two sentences"} where edits_needed values are none, few, some or many.
